bar.purpose: Bars 2px high or less, such as the read-timer track.

hairline.purpose: Preview pages, the model progress bar, the tab underline.

sm.purpose: Fields, notices, choice tiles, icon buttons, preview well, diff blocks.

control-lg.purpose: Large (46px) and full-width buttons; see The Pills-Are-Small Rule.

pill.purpose: Controls 38px tall or less: standard and small buttons, chips, tags.

themes.dark: @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) overrides the same custom properties; frontmatter carries them as <token>-dark

display-compact.purpose: Responsive variant of display: page titles at 860px and below.

wordmark.purpose: CVMaker wordmark beside the violet tile.

wordmark-compact.purpose: Responsive variant of wordmark at 480px and below.

ui-sm.purpose: Small UI size (0.875rem): small-button labels (600), check labels, chips (500), notices, status row, dialog footer, diff text. Weight follows the element.

title.purpose: Panel and section titles, including the editable section-title field.

body.purpose: All running text and field content.

meta.purpose: Dates, counts, status text; muted, tabular.

micro.purpose: Tab step numerals, diff labels, Hidden tag.

shadows.name: pop
shadows.purpose: Dialogs and the focused skip link.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: A panel or entry while dragged; settles away over 0.5s after drop.

shadows.name: paper
shadows.purpose: PDF preview pages in the recessed preview well.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: All movement: tab underline, panel and dialog entry, chevrons, settle.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Colour and border transitions on buttons, fields, tabs.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Drop settle on sortable panels and entries.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion, entries fall back to fade-in; transforms, settle and pulse are dropped; the 2s read timer and progress remain.

narrative.overview:
CVMaker is a writing desk for one document. Neutral surfaces recede, the user's own words are set in an editorial display serif, and a single indigo-violet carries every action, focus ring, active state and highlight. Nothing else on screen is coloured, so the violet always means "this is live" or "this is yours to act on", and the CV content reads as the most important thing in the room.

Density is calm rather than sparse: white panels with hairline borders and 12px corners sit on a near-white ground (near-black, faintly violet ground in dark), stacked in a single column on My Profile and paired side by side on the Keyword Extractor and CV Generator. Depth is mostly tonal; shadows appear only on things that float (dialogs, a dragged panel, the preview page). Motion is short and settling: panels fade up, dialogs fade and rise, chips fade in, a dropped panel exhales a shadow.

Light and dark are equal citizens and follow the system setting; every token below has a dark counterpart (the `-dark` keys), tuned so the accent lightens to a soft lavender and the accent-on-accent ink flips to a deep violet-black.
keyCharacteristics: One accent hue (indigo-violet), used only for actions, focus, the active tab, matched keywords, selection and the brand tile.
Libre Caslon Display 400 for page, panel, section and dialog titles and the wordmark; Manrope for everything else.
1px hairlines and tonal surface steps instead of shadows at rest.
Pill-shaped buttons and chips against 8px fields and 12px panels.
Section titles are editable in place yet read as headings until touched.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Indigo-violet is the only decorative or interactive hue. If an element is coloured and it is not an action, focus, the active state, a matched keyword, selection or the brand mark, it should not be coloured.

rules.name: The Semantic Quarantine Rule
rules.body: Danger and caution colours appear only as status (errors, warnings, a destructive hover). They never tag sections, decorate headers or fill buttons at rest.

rules.name: The Two-Violet Rule
rules.body: Fills use `accent`; text uses `accent-text`. Never set body-size text in the fill violet on a light surface.

rules.name: The Caslon Is For Names Rule
rules.body: The serif sets titles only: page, panel, section, dialog, choice names and the wordmark, always at weight 400. Never use it for body copy, labels, buttons or numbers.

rules.name: The No Faux-Bold Display Rule
rules.body: Libre Caslon Display ships one weight; hierarchy among serif titles comes from size, never weight or caps.

rules.name: The Lifted-Only Rule
rules.body: A shadow means the thing is floating (dialog, dragged panel, paper). Resting panels, buttons and chips stay flat; the primary button carries only a 1px contact shadow.

rules.name: The Pills-Are-Small Rule
rules.body: The full pill is for controls 38px tall or less. A large button (46px) or a full-width button takes 10px corners, because a long pill reads as a capsule rather than a button.

dos: Do reserve indigo-violet for actions, focus, the active tab underline, matched keywords, selection and the brand tile.
Do set page, panel, section and dialog titles in Libre Caslon Display 400 with slight negative tracking (-0.01em to -0.015em).
Do separate surfaces with 1px hairlines and the Ground / Surface / Recess steps before reaching for a shadow.
Do give every interactive element a visible 2px violet focus outline (or the field focus halo).
Do keep motion short and eased with `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`, 150 to 250ms, and fall back to fades only under reduced motion.
Do ship both light and dark values for any new token.
Do use 16px stroke icons at 2px stroke in currentColor, inlined as SVG.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue, brown tones, or red as decoration; red is for errors and destructive hover only.
Don't tag sections with per-section colours.
Don't add call numbers, a catalogue rail or a job-match side panel.
Don't use the serif for body text, buttons, labels or figures.
Don't shadow panels, buttons or chips at rest.
Don't hide the move up/down buttons entirely; keep them quiet at 55% until their row is engaged.
Don't wash the ground grey; it stays near-white in light and near-black in dark.
